hunks.sol: So I knew one thing very well: the worse the situation, the more clearheaded I had to be.

hunks.sol: And now, four days after arriving in Xining, clearheaded judgment and a few more pieces of information had finally led me to a conclusion.

hunks.baseline: I opened my mouth to the guy who was about as useful as a pathetic little toe.
hunks.sol: I addressed the guy who was more like a shabby little toe.

hunks.sol: Potala Palace’s rise at precisely this moment also meant we could no longer count on support from Sichuan.

hunks.baseline: “Now that even the Great Nation’s military vessels guarding the Yangtze’s tributaries have been wiped out, the river routes through the Central Plains are basically in their hands for the time being.”
hunks.sol: “Now that even the Great Nation’s military vessels guarding the Yangtze’s tributaries have been wiped out, the waterways through the Central Plains are practically in their hands for the time being.”

hunks.baseline: I wanted to deny it, but the truth was impossible to deny now.
hunks.sol: I wanted to deny it, but I couldn’t anymore.

hunks.baseline: The battle with the Yangtze River Channel League had dealt it a terrible blow, but if that were enough to make it lose control of the entire Yangtze, it never could have claimed to rule the world in the first place.
hunks.sol: The battle with the Yangtze River Channel League had dealt it a terrible blow, but if that alone were enough to make it lose control of the entire Yangtze, it never could have claimed to rule the world in the first place.

hunks.baseline: “Time. It’s a question of time, isn’t it?”
hunks.sol: “Time. Time is the problem, isn’t it?”

hunks.baseline: “The time they’ve gained, however brief, will be more damaging to us than anything.”
hunks.sol: “Even that little time they’ve gained will be more damaging to us than anything.”

hunks.baseline: By the time the Great Nation invoked its authority to requisition ships wherever it could and gathered its naval forces from across the land, it would be too late.
hunks.sol: By the time the Great Nation invoked its authority to requisition every ship it could and gathered its naval forces from across the land, it would already be too late.

hunks.baseline: By then, Qinghai Province—no, Xining itself—would be completely surrounded, front and back.
hunks.sol: By then, Qinghai—no, Xining itself—would be completely surrounded, front and back.

hunks.baseline: At Jeok Cheongang’s question, I answered,
hunks.sol: I answered Jeok Cheongang.

hunks.baseline: “Hah. They’re swarming in like a pack of dogs. Then again, numbers are about the only thing those dark-path bastards have to brag about.”
hunks.sol: “Hah. They’re coming in packs like dogs. Then again, numbers are about the only thing those dark-path bastards have to brag about.”

hunks.baseline: “If it were just numbers, that would be much better. Take out their heads, and the rest would collapse on its own.”
hunks.sol: “If it were just numbers, that would be much better. Take out their leaders, and the rest would collapse on its own.”

hunks.baseline: As was true everywhere, the dark-path figures and the unorthodox factions were especially dependent on having someone at their center.
hunks.sol: As was true everywhere, dark-path figures and unorthodox factions were especially dependent on the people at their center.

hunks.baseline: Their nature was to gather and scatter around individuals who became the head of the group through overwhelming strength and the ability to command others.
hunks.sol: They gathered and scattered around individuals who became their leaders through overwhelming strength and the ability to command others.

hunks.baseline: “Of course. Those cowards have seen for themselves that the dark arts they’d only heard about are real. They’ll be even more inclined to tuck their tails between their legs.”
hunks.sol: “Of course. Those cowards have seen for themselves that the dark arts they’d only heard about are real. They’ll tuck their tails between their legs even tighter.”

hunks.baseline: And right in the heart of the Central Plains.
hunks.sol: Right in the heart of the Central Plains.

hunks.baseline: The existence of Moving Formations had always been a source of concern for the Murim of the Central Plains. But having that concern become reality was another matter entirely.
hunks.sol: The existence of Moving Formations had always worried the Central Plains Murim. Having that fear become reality was another matter entirely.

hunks.baseline: It seemed even the great sects like the Zhuge Clan and Wudang couldn’t ignore the problem.
hunks.sol: It seemed even great sects like the Zhuge Clan and Wudang couldn’t ignore it.

hunks.baseline: Even they, more or less the dominant powers of Hubei’s Murim, had chosen to avoid a direct confrontation.
hunks.sol: Though they all but ruled Hubei’s Murim, even they had chosen to avoid a direct confrontation.

hunks.baseline: I’d heard that the Zhuge Clan had gone so far as to flee to Mount Wudang, abandoning the family home where they’d put down roots for hundreds of years.
hunks.sol: I’d heard the Zhuge Clan had gone so far as to flee to Mount Wudang, leaving behind the family home where they’d put down roots for hundreds of years.

hunks.baseline: We hadn’t known each other for all that long, but from what I’d seen of him while I was in Hubei, he was a good man.
hunks.sol: We hadn’t known each other all that long, but from what I’d seen of him while I was in Hubei, he was a good man.

hunks.baseline: Like a rock in a raging current, he was carefree yet steadfast, with the ability to back up that resolve.
hunks.sol: Like a rock in a raging current, he was free-spirited yet steadfast, with the ability to back up that resolve.

hunks.baseline: And most of all, he was a man who deserved to be called a Great Hero.
hunks.sol: And more than anything, he deserved to be called a Great Hero.

hunks.baseline: The Murim Alliance—a single banner raised by all of them.
hunks.sol: The Murim Alliance—the single banner they had all raised together.

hunks.baseline: I wanted to look each of them in the eye, men who never hesitated to call themselves righteous, and ask:
hunks.sol: I wanted to look those people, who had never hesitated to call themselves righteous, straight in the eye and ask:

hunks.baseline: Was this the great cause they spoke of, the reason they couldn’t stop the traitors heading west?
hunks.sol: Was their so-called great cause the reason they couldn’t stop the traitors heading west?

hunks.baseline: Crack.
hunks.sol: *Crack.*
The bones in my fist popped. I hadn’t realized how tightly I’d clenched it.

hunks.baseline: Just then, my clenched fist popped. Jeok Cheongang, who had been watching me with a solemn gaze, spoke up.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang, who had been watching me with a somber gaze, spoke.

hunks.baseline: As if agreeing, Bow Saint nodded quietly. Both had reached heights martial artists could scarcely dream of, and yet even they had to consider the possibility of defeat. That was how dire things were.
hunks.sol: Bow Saint, who had been watching in silence, nodded as if she agreed. Both had reached heights most martial artists wouldn’t dare dream of, yet even they had to consider the possibility of defeat. That was how dire things were.

hunks.baseline: “In a situation like this, not a soul under heaven could blame you for choosing to live and fight another day.”
hunks.sol: “In a situation like this, not a soul under heaven could blame you for withdrawing to fight another day.”

hunks.baseline: *Live and fight another day.*
hunks.sol: *Withdraw to fight another day.*

hunks.baseline: I met Jeok Cheongang’s gaze and continued,
hunks.sol: I met Jeok Cheongang’s gaze and continued.

hunks.baseline: “Even if I chose to live and fight another day—no, if I ran away—they’d have no right to criticize me.”
hunks.sol: “Even if I withdrew to fight another day—no, if I ran away—they’d have no right to criticize me.”

hunks.baseline: “Even so, it wouldn’t matter. If anyone dared to criticize you, I’d personally rip out his tongue. If anyone pointed a finger at you, I’d turn it to ash.”
hunks.sol: “Even if they did, it wouldn’t matter. If anyone dared to criticize you, I’d personally rip out his tongue. If anyone pointed a finger at you, I’d turn it to ash.”

hunks.baseline: “Because if we leave, Qinghai is finished. The countless civilians living in Xining won’t even have time to escape.”
hunks.sol: “Because if we leave, Qinghai is finished. The countless civilians staying in Xining won’t even have time to escape.”

hunks.baseline: “If we meet our deaths here, it may not just be Qinghai that falls into their hands. It could be the whole world.”
hunks.sol: “If we fight to the death here, it may not just be Qinghai that falls into their hands. It could be the whole world.”

hunks.baseline: The Three Saints and Ten Kings were symbols of the Murim world, and its strongest forces.
hunks.sol: The Three Saints and Ten Kings were symbols of the Murim world, and its strongest fighters.

hunks.baseline: It was embarrassing to admit, but I, too, had become a symbol of sorts.
hunks.sol: It was embarrassing to admit, but I, too, had become something of a symbol.

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang let out a sigh as he looked at me in silence.
hunks.sol: As I fell silent, Jeok Cheongang went on with something like a sigh.

hunks.baseline: “The world has already looked away. The Nine Sects and One Gang, the Five Great Families, the Murim Alliance—they’ve all turned their backs. And you still plan to make such a foolhardy choice?”
hunks.sol: “The world has already looked away. The Nine Sects and One Gang, the Five Great Families, the Murim Alliance—they’ve all turned their backs. And you still mean to make such a foolish choice?”

hunks.baseline: “Even so, we have to.”
hunks.sol: “Even so, I have to.”

hunks.baseline: “No. Because everyone has turned away and abandoned us, we have to do it even more.”
hunks.sol: “No. Because everyone has looked away and turned their backs, I have to do it all the more.”

hunks.baseline: The light it throws off as it breaks into dozens of pieces is more brilliant than ever.
hunks.sol: The light it gives off as it breaks into dozens of pieces is more brilliant than ever.

hunks.baseline: That is what it means to shatter like jade.
hunks.sol: That is jade shattering.

hunks.baseline: That is why it is called jade’s shattering.
hunks.sol: That is why it is called jade shattering.

hunks.baseline: It is so brilliant, you forget the word *destruction*.
hunks.sol: Because it shines so brightly that you forget it is being destroyed.

hunks.baseline: It would rather break than be defiled.
hunks.sol: Because it breaks rather than be defiled.

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang stared at me, eyes wide. I continued, slowly, but clearly.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang stared at me, eyes wide. I continued, slowly but clearly.

hunks.baseline: “I haven’t. But I know that jade already covered in grime can lose its value, at least for a while.”
hunks.sol: “I haven’t. But I know that jade already covered in filth loses its value, at least for a while.”

hunks.baseline: Even so, the essence of the jade remained.
hunks.sol: Even then, the jade’s true nature doesn’t disappear.

hunks.baseline: Even if it looked like nothing but dirt on the outside, there was still light hidden within.
hunks.sol: It might look like nothing but filth, but the light is still hidden within it.

hunks.baseline: But seeing filth cover its beautiful surface, no one would reach out to touch it.
hunks.sol: Yet no one who sees its beautiful surface covered in grime will want to touch it.

hunks.baseline: Not unless a sudden downpour washed the jade clean.
hunks.sol: Not unless a sudden downpour washes the jade clean.

hunks.baseline: Not unless someone who remembered what it once looked like found it and carefully wiped it off.
hunks.sol: Not unless someone who remembers what it looks like finds it and carefully wipes it off.

hunks.baseline: Even if it ended in death, I couldn’t lose that brilliant light I’d had from the beginning.
hunks.sol: Even if it ended in death, I couldn’t let that original brilliance fade.

hunks.baseline: I had to make everyone remember. I had to make them realize what mattered most—the thing they’d briefly forgotten while hiding behind excuses about the greater good and worrying about what they might lose.
hunks.sol: I had to make everyone remember. I had to make them realize what mattered most—the thing they’d briefly forgotten amid excuses about the great cause and fears of what they might lose.

hunks.baseline: There was still far too much left to do before I could face a final moment of brilliance.
hunks.sol: There was still far too much to do before I faced that brilliant final moment.

hunks.baseline: Just then, as the meaning of those two words rang through my heart and drew nearer than ever, Jeok Cheongang—head bowed, lost in thought amid the heavy silence—suddenly spoke.
hunks.sol: The meaning of that name, now so much closer, echoed in my mind. Then, amid the heavy silence, Jeok Cheongang lifted his head from his thoughts and spoke.

hunks.baseline: He muttered as if speaking to himself, then raised his head.
hunks.sol: He muttered as if speaking to himself, then raised his head fully.

hunks.baseline: The gaze that had been sunk deep in memories of that day, not so long ago, began to shine.
hunks.sol: His gaze, drawn back to that day in the not-so-distant past, began to shine.
